Developing Monitoring Frameworks & Systems ·        Establish Key Performance Indicators (KPIs): Define and develop project-specific KPIs for time, cost, quality, and procurement. ·        Develop Workflows and Systems: Design and deploy reporting templates, field data collection mechanisms, and monitoring workflows. ·        Standardization: Apply unified methodologies and best practices for tracking progress across all company projects. 2. Progress & Financial Performance Tracking ·        Track Site Progress: Measure actual vs. planned progress (Planned vs. Actual) and identify variances. ·        Monitor Costs and Budgets: Track expenditure, cash flow, and apply Earned Value Management (EVM). ·        Change Management: Track variation orders and change requests, evaluating their impact on the project schedule and budget. 3. Procurement & Supply Chain Monitoring ·        Track Purchase Orders and Deliveries: Monitor the status of Purchase Requests (PRs), Purchase Orders (POs), and site delivery schedules to prevent timeline delays. ·        Submittals Tracking: Monitor approval status for shop drawings, material samples, and technical submittals from the consultant. ·        Site Material and Inventory Tracking: Verify that delivered materials comply with specifications and track Goods Received Notes (GRNs). 4. Team Leadership & Organizational Coordination ·        Lead the Monitoring Team: Direct, mentor, and assign tasks to monitoring specialists and data analysts within the office. ·        Cross-Departmental Coordination: Act as a bridge between Project Management, Procurement, Finance, and Warehousing to ensure seamless data flow. ·        Continuous Improvement: Provide recommendations to enhance execution efficiency and document Lessons Learned for future projects.
